name: Flores Island
tagline: Colorful island town on the lake
description: The tiny historic island town on Lake Peten Itza, connected by causeway to the mainland. Cobbled streets, pastel buildings, lakeside restaurants and hostels make it the charming tourist heart and main base for Tikal trips.
bestFor: Travellers wanting lakeside charm, cafes and easy Tikal access on foot

name: Santa Elena
tagline: Mainland hub with services and banks
description: The larger mainland town across the causeway, where the banks, supermarkets, bus terminal and hospital are located. Less scenic than the island but cheaper and more practical for longer stays and everyday errands.
bestFor: Budget and longer-stay travellers needing banks, groceries and transport links

name: San Miguel
tagline: Quiet lakeside village across the water
description: A small tranquil village on the north shore of Lake Peten Itza, reached by a short boat crossing from Flores. It offers quiet guesthouses, a small beach, a lookout trail and a slower, local pace.
bestFor: Travellers seeking calm lake views and a slower village base near town

name: San Benito
description: The larger, busier town merging with Santa Elena on the mainland, home to markets, cheap eateries and the most affordable housing in the area. Purely functional and local, with little tourism but strong value.
bestFor: Budget nomads prioritising low rent over charm and tourist amenities
